question.text: In the standard private-equity deal pipeline described in Ch 11, at which stage does the PE firm first require the investee company to sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA)?

answer.text: After signing the term sheet, before virtual data-room access
After the Shareholders' Agreement is executed
Only at the Final Investment Memorandum stage
After gaining initial interest in the start-up, before examining confidential records

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.1.3.2 (PE deal structure), the NDA is signed immediately after deal sourcing and initial interest so the team can assess and examine the start-up's records before proceeding to initial due diligence. Skipping the NDA risks the firm receiving price-sensitive info without confidentiality protection. The Trap: Option A puts the NDA after the term sheet — but the term sheet itself requires prior info access. Option C (FIM stage) is far too late. Option D (post-SHA) is absurd — NDA goes at the start, not end. Cross-Exam Context: Same NDA-first sequence tested in X-A/X-B for Investment Advisers on institutional mandates and in XV for Research Analysts receiving non-public corporate briefings. Manager's Pro-Tip: Standard market NDAs now include a 'residual knowledge' carve-out and a specific tail period (2-3 years). Push back on any NDA that restricts the fund from investing in 'similar' companies — that's an anti-competitive clause, not confidentiality.
